newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan capital to punish adults for buying teen sex.
newsitem.headline: Japan capital to punish adults for buying teen sex.

text.p: In a bid to stamp out rising teenage prostitution in the Japanese capital, Tokyo authorities on Thursday started a legal process that would punish adults who buy sex from minors.

An advisory panel of the Tokyo Metropolitan District recommended the capital bring its laws in line with most local governments in Japan by prohibiting adults from engaging in "obscene" acts with children under 18.
Tokyo and Nagano in central Japan, site of the 1998 Winter Olympic Games, are the only local governments without such laws.
"I believe an ordinance will be an effective means to limit teenage prostitution," Tokyo Governor Yukio Aoshima told reporters.
The new bill would punish only those who make payments in cash or gifts in exchange for sex.
Ordinances in other areas prohibit indecent acts with children regardless of whether any payment is made.
Details of the punishment have yet to be determined.
Tokyo decided against issuing the ordinance nine years ago due to what it said was the ambiguity of the term "obscene" and in consideration of privacy of individuals.
But an increasing number of cases where young school girls have turned to part-time prostitution has set off demands for the issue to be reconsidered.
A survey by the Tokyo government last year found about a quarter of female students aged from 12 to 15 years had taken part in telephone chat clubs believed to be a major vehicle for prostitution.
Japan, which for centuries had a highly institutionalised prostitution industry, in 1956 passed a law prohibiting formal brothels and open solicitation.
However, many forms of prostitution continue to thrive.
